abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are central to cellular function, disease gene identification, and therapeutic targeting. Human Integrated Protein-Protein Interaction rEference (HIPPIE) provides a confidence-scored reference network of experimentally supported human PPIs by integrating evidence from multiple resources and assigning reliability scores to individual interactions. Here, we present HIPPIE 3.0, a major update that substantially expands the scale and scope of the resource. HIPPIE now contains ~1.2 million experimentally supported PPIs, a fourfold increase since the last major release, including 71 000 isoform-specific interactions. Beyond interaction data, HIPPIE captures the underlying experimental search space by incorporating non-interacting protein pairs experimentally tested, and provides large-scale cross-species conservation annotations. This release expands the catalog of experimental methods, recalibrates confidence scores, and introduces a redesigned web interface that improves data access and exploration. To support machine learning applications, HIPPIE 3.0 provides high-confidence positive interactions and negative training datasets, together with tools for generating sequence-similarity- and degree-aware benchmark splits to reduce performance inflation caused by data leakage. By combining an expanded experimental interactome with benchmark-generation strategies tailored for PPI prediction, HIPPIE 3.0 serves as both a reference interactome and a platform for evaluating PPI prediction methods. HIPPIE 3.0 is freely available at hippie-db.net.
